entire_current_literal.source_text: Intuition and example. In the plane $x^\top y=\|x\|\,\|y\|\cos\theta$: the inner product measures alignment. For $x=(1,2)$, $y=(3,-1)$: $x^\top y=1$, $\|x\|=\sqrt5$, $\|y\|=\sqrt{10}$, $\theta\approx81.9^\circ$. With $M=\mathrm{diag}(1,4)$ (coordinate 2 counts double): $\langle x,y\rangle_M=3-8=-5$, $\|x\|_M=\sqrt{17}$, $\|y\|_M=\sqrt{13}$, an obtuse angle. Which vectors are long or perpendicular depends on the inner product.
